prompt:
Feature: ignore untranslated plurals when seeding foods and units.

The food and unit seeders (mealie.repos.seed.seeders) load a locale's seed file and store every entry's plural_name (and, for units, plural_abbreviation) as is. Crowdin cannot store an empty translation, so for a term that has no plural in the target language translators either repeat the singular or leave the English plural untouched. Seeding ja-JP or ko-KR then creates foods whose plural is their singular, or an English word ("cups" on the Korean "컵"), and the ingredient display pluralises with the wrong word.

Expected:
1. Two pure functions in mealie.lang.locale_config, keyword-only arguments:
   - resolve_plural(*, source_singular, source_plural, singular, plural) -> str | None, where source_singular and source_plural are the same term in the source locale, en-US. Rules: an empty or missing plural, or a plural equal to the singular, gives None ("garlic"/"" with "ajo"/"" or "ajo"/None; "teaspoon"/"teaspoons" with "茶匙"/"茶匙"). A translated singular (one that differs from the source singular) whose plural still equals the source plural gives None: "cup"/"cups" with "컵"/"cups", "pound"/"lbs" with "libra"/"lbs", and also "eggplant"/"eggplants" with "aubergine"/"eggplants", even though that plural might be legitimate. Otherwise the plural is kept: "onion"/"onions" with "cebolla"/"cebollas" gives "cebollas", and a plural the translation adds although the source has none, "celery"/"" with "sellerie"/"sellerien", gives "sellerien".
   - resolve_food_plural(*, source_singular, source_plural, singular, plural, locale) -> str | None. For a locale whose LOCALE_CONFIG entry has plural_food_handling NEVER (ja-JP and zh-TW among them) it is always None, even for a term that is not translated at all ("onion"/"onions" with "onion"/"onions" and ja-JP). For any other locale, for None, and for an unknown code such as "xx-XX", it applies resolve_plural ("onion"/"onions" with "zwiebel"/"zwiebeln" gives "zwiebeln" for de-DE, en-US, None and "xx-XX").
2. The seeders use them. AbstractSeeder gets source_locale = "en-US" and a cached source_data property holding the en-US file, loaded once per seeder. The unit seeder resolves each unit's plural_name against the same key in the source file (name and plural_name) and its plural_abbreviation against the source's abbreviation and plural_abbreviation; the food seeder resolves each food's plural_name against the same label key and food key in the source file, passing the locale being seeded to resolve_food_plural. A key the source file does not have is compared with the entry itself, that is, treated as untranslated. Everything else about seeding (de-duplication by localized name, labels, descriptions, abbreviations) is unchanged.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
title: feat: ignore plurals when they're not translated (#8516)
